messages.subject: Moving linearly through data
parts:
Dear Shiny, I am extremely impressed by the package and am spending a lot of time reading over the tutorials and whatever help files I can find.  I have a question which has probably been answered a dozen times but I am afraid I need to make it again.

I would like to move linearly through a list of data sets with each click of the user's button pushing the list one item further.

I know I can do this with various other selectors such as sliders and drop boxes but I would like the progression to be linear and one way more like a slideshow that is out of the hands of the user.

The user clicks the action button and it moves forward.  I can do this of course with globals but that means that any user can push the counter forward.  I figure this is just a matter of targeting the right environment as far as modifying variables within it but I have been having difficulty doing that.

My UI code is:    
actionButton("next", "Next!"),
h5(textOutput("clicks"))

My server:

clicks <- 0
  shinyServer(function(input, output) { 
    output$clicks <- renderText({
      input$goButton
      eval.parent(clicks <- clicks+1)
  })
}

PS: Is there a list somewhere of all of the visitor values that are currently available to the server such as user IP?

Thanks so much!
Francis

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Moving linearly through data
parts:
h5(textOutput("clicks"))

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  values <- reactiveValues(clicks = 0)
  observe({
    if (input$next1 == 0)
      return()
    isolate({
      values$clicks <- values$clicks + 1
    })
  })

  output$clicks <- renderText({ values$clicks })
})

Instead of defining a number directly, I define a reactiveValues() object called "values" and put the clicks on there. This makes it easy for other render* functions and reactive expressions to react when the number of clicks changes.

Also, I put the handler code for the actionButton in an observe/check-for-0/isolate pattern. This is the usual way of dealing with actionButtons (I know it's unwieldy, I'd like to change that soon).

Hope that helps.
